doc.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Lifelong friendship with Gerald Wilson
summary: Young says he and Gerald Wilson are as close as ever, and Wilson's college music and collegiate scores helped him become a stronger reader.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Let‘s talk about your long friendship with Gerald Wilson. We know it goes all the way back to when you were in Jimmie Lunceford‘s band.
Or maybe, I think Chick Carter, did we talk about Chick Carter? Was he is Chick Carter‘s band together? No?
Yeah, okay, so you now you‘re 90 years young and you‘re still playing with somebody you started playing with when you were just a kid.
It is. And we‘re just as close now as we were then.
What‘s the key to such a close relationship?
[Laughs] That‘s a good question, how can I answer that? I don‘t know…
Well, let‘s say a lot of respect, mutual respect. Mutual respect, you respect one another.
Oh yeah, we have mutual respect for one another, that‘s true, that kind of helps, and then Gerald, Gerald helped me a lot. He was instrumental in getting me into Jimmie Lunceford‘s band.

And we had played in Chick Carter‘s band and we had done some things, but Gerald had come out of Cass Tech in Detroit and he had a lot of, music and things for people for beginners and different things in other words, a lot of music from the college. And he gave me a lot of that, and it helped me in reading and becoming a stronger reader I believe that. You know, because I hadn‘t… the way I come up I didn‘t have the musical background like he got coming from the college and everything. You see? And that really helped me, and afterwards when he got into Lunceford‘s band well he told Lunceford about me, got me in, and just moved me on up, that‘s the way it happened. It‘s hard for

me to explain that because what we did, like when we were with Chick Carter‘s band and everything, we use to practice and fool around on the horn and everything… I think, well actually I could play as good as Gerald did I mean, and he just come out of college and everything, but he had a different, he had more background than me in other words, that‘s hard to explain, but that‘s why he‘s such a great writer today. He had a very strong background, musical background. I never had that. I wish I had got that, because I might be following up the line then. You know what I‘m saying.
